- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.35) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price drop is sharp.  
- After a price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 80+), model often fails to recognize it; apply slight upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish; reduce first 3–5 forecast points by 1–2% to align with observed decay.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.68, -0.38, +0.68), model often misreads momentum; apply smoothing filter to sentiment-weighted average before adjusting forecast.
